                        Recording guide
                        Daily attendance marks

                        Blank means Present. Use T for Tardy, E for Excused, or CC/X for Absent.

                        Absences and monthly remarks

                        Reasons are optional. Type one under any learner marked Absent or Excused (E). Use Monthly Remarks for NLS, Transferred Out, or Transferred In; select the exact status date.

                        Holidays and no-class dates

                        Mark dates as Holiday/No Class; the register will display NC for every learner.

                        Summary Of Attendance

                        Totals are calculated from saved attendance records.

                        Workbook view: pick a sheet tab at the bottom to see one month, or All Months for the full-year totals.

                        All Months

                        No students in this class

                        Add or import students before recording attendance.

                        How totals are counted

                        Present and Tardy each count as one present day; Absent counts as one absent day. Each recorded month shows separate Present and Absent totals, followed by overall totals.

                        Excused, unmarked days, Holiday/No Class dates, and locked status dates are not counted.

                        Percentage Score = (Raw Score ÷ Total Items) × 100   |   MPS = Sum of all learners’ percentage scores ÷ Number of Learners

                        DepEd Memorandum No. 160, s. 2012 descriptive equivalents: 96–100 = Mastered; 86–95 = Closely Approximating Mastery; 66–85 = Moving Towards Mastery; 35–65 = Average; 15–34 = Low; 5–14 = Very Low; 0–4 = Absolutely No Mastery.

                        DIFFICULTY INDEX (Df) REPORT

                        Item No.Number of Correct ResponsesDifficulty Index (Df)InterpretationRecommended Action

                        Summary

                        Total Items Analyzed0
                        Number of Easy Items0
                        Number of Moderate Items0
                        Number of Difficult Items0

                        Formula: Df = Number of Correct Responses ÷ Total Number of Learners. Interpretation: 0.81–1.00 Very Easy (Revise / Make more challenging); 0.20–0.80 Moderate / Ideal (Retain); 0.00–0.19 Very Difficult (Revise / Reteach competency).

                        ITEM ANALYSIS REPORT – TERM EXAMINATION and SUMMATIVE TEST

                        Item No.Learning CompetencyDifficulty Index (Df)Discrimination Index (Ds)Distractor Analysis (for multiple-choice items)Remarks/Action

                        Summary

                        Number of Items Analyzed0
                        Number of Items Retained0
                        Number of Items to Revise0
                        Number of Items to Discard0
                        Least Mastered Competencies 

                        Item-level response data are not available. Enter item-level data when available; blank index fields are intentionally preserved.

                        Formulas: Df = learners who answered correctly ÷ total learners. Ds = proportion correct in the Upper Group − proportion correct in the Lower Group. Upper and Lower Groups are the top and bottom 27% by total test score.

                        Interpretation: Df 0.20–0.80 and Ds ≥ 0.30 = Retain; Df 0.20–0.80 and Ds 0.20–0.29 = Revise; Df below 0.20, Ds below 0.20, or negative Ds = Revise or Discard; Df above 0.80 with Ds ≥ 0.30 = Retain if still useful. Distractors should attract more learners from the Lower Group; non-functional distractors should be flagged.

                        RMA (Rapid Mathematics Assessment)

                        Record BOSY, MOSY, and EOSY math results, review mastery, and track learner progress.

                        Template scoring: total score is the sum of weighted item points (items may be worth 1, 2, or 3 points); percentage score = total score ÷ the selected grade-level maximum (Grade 4: 13, Grade 5: 32, Grade 6: 50) × 100. Levelling uses the template’s grade-specific raw-score cutoffs. Content and cognitive domain benchmarks are met at 75% or higher. A learner is counted as assessed only when an assessment date is entered.

                        What's new

                        Developer changes included in this version of GraceDesk.

                        Version 1.0.61

                        • Teacher profile information is organized into Basic Info, School Info, Background Information, and SALN Records tabs.
                        • SF 10 now synchronizes the selected learner's three term grades from SF 9, including Music and Arts and Physical Education and Health.
                        • School and classroom details are filled from the teacher profile for the matching classified grade.
                        • SF 10 final ratings, General Average, and Passed/Failed remarks are generated from SF 9 grades and locked against manual edits.
                        • SF 10 follows the three-term curriculum and has a more organized toolbar.

                            About this app

                            GraceDesk — Every record, one desk. This application was designed by a Grade Adviser of Balintawak Elementary School to support teachers in managing classroom records and learner information more efficiently. By consolidating essential record-keeping functions into a single platform, the app aims to reduce administrative workload and promote more effective classroom management.

                            The development of this application was assisted by AI-based tools; however, full responsibility for its content, operation, and use rests with the developer and its users. This application is independently developed and is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or representative of the Department of Education (DepEd).

                            Disclaimer

                            AI-assisted development does not guarantee that every feature, calculation, report, or recommendation is complete or error-free. Always check information against original records and current DepEd policies before relying on it, sharing it, or submitting an official report. The app is a record-keeping aid, not a substitute for a teacher’s professional judgment or official guidance.

                            Users are responsible for keeping learner and family information accurate, confidential, and secure. Do not enter information you are not authorized to manage, and promptly correct errors you find.

                            Terms and conditions

                            • Use the portal only for legitimate classroom, school, or parent purposes and only for information you are authorized to access.
                            • Protect your sign-in credentials, keep devices secure, and do not share another person’s account or confidential learner information.
                            • Review and verify records, grades, calculations, and generated documents before using or distributing them. You are responsible for maintaining appropriate backups of your records.
                            • Do not misuse the portal, attempt to access another class or account without permission, or use it in a way that violates applicable laws, school policies, or learner privacy requirements.
                            • The app is provided as a classroom aid. The creator makes no guarantee of uninterrupted availability or error-free results and is not responsible for decisions made without independently checking the information.

                            By choosing “I understand and agree,” you acknowledge this notice and agree to use the app under these terms.
